## Purpose

The `deepagents` runtime **adapter layer**: it turns a `create_deep_agent` LangGraph graph
into the exact streaming/event contract the sibling `backend/agents/execution_engine`
sequencer and the frontend WebSocket already consume (`DeepAgentRunner`), and supplies
everything that graph needs to run safely — model selection ([model_factory.build_model](../../backend/app/agents/model_factory.py)), a
disk-backed per-run sandbox ([sandbox.RunSandbox](../../backend/app/agents/sandbox.py)), durable HITL checkpointing
([checkpointer.py](../../backend/app/agents/checkpointer.py)), and prototype-output validation ([static_check.py](../../backend/app/agents/static_check.py) / [render_check.py](../../backend/app/agents/render_check.py)).

It also hosts the free-chat sequencer ([chat_runner.ChatRunner](../../backend/app/agents/chat_runner.py)), the `/flowin-handoff` agents
(`handoff/`), and several app-side `CapabilityRegistry` plugins (validators, the local
git/exec runtime, the repo symbol index, MCP client) that need a heavy dependency the kernel
must never import directly.

## Shape

**Every model call in this module funnels through exactly two sanctioned paths**, both built
on [model_factory.build_model](../../backend/app/agents/model_factory.py):

- The adapter itself — [deep_agent_runner.DeepAgentRunner](../../backend/app/agents/deep_agent_runner.py): wraps one
  `create_deep_agent(...)` graph per agent invocation; `astream_events()` maps LangGraph's
  `astream_events` output onto `{chunk, usage, tool_call, tool_result, done, gate, error}`,
  the vocabulary [engine.py](../../backend/agents/execution_engine/engine.py)'s `_run_agent` loop expects. `_ToolFilterMiddleware` always
  strips the library's `task` sub-agent-dispatch tool (and, for text-only agents, the whole
  built-in fs suite); `_BedrockCachePointsMiddleware` places the Bedrock `cache_control`
  Anthropic-only caching misses. `_gate_payload()` detects a paused
  `HumanInTheLoopMiddleware` interrupt post-loop (interrupts don't surface as stream events).

- Model + reliability — [model_factory.build_model()](../../backend/app/agents/model_factory.py): the one place that picks ChatAnthropic
  (local, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) vs `ChatBedrockConverse` (prod) vs `ChatMistralAI` (fallback),
  and owns botocore timeout/retry tuning. [cached_invoke.py](../../backend/app/agents/cached_invoke.py) is the parallel one-shot path for
  callers that don't need a full agent graph (the handoff classifier/test/compliance agents) —
  same `build_model`, same Bedrock cache-point logic, so a direct `ainvoke` still gets caching
  + counted tokens (`[ISS-033](../cards/20260704-2146-ISS-033.md)`).

- Isolation — [sandbox.RunSandbox](../../backend/app/agents/sandbox.py): a traversal-proof `<RUNS_ROOT>/<user>/<run>/` dir the
  graph's `FilesystemBackend` is rooted at; `serialize_sandbox_deliverable()` walks it back
  into the legacy `filename:`-block deliverable string byte-for-byte. [runtime/local.py](../../backend/app/agents/runtime/local.py)
  (`LocalSandboxRuntime`, registered `runtime_env:local`) is the sibling that owns the
  git-subprocess surface (clone/branch/diff) for repo-backed workflows, with `exec` off by
  default.

- Durability — [checkpointer.get_checkpointer()](../../backend/app/agents/checkpointer.py): `AsyncPostgresSaver` in prod, `InMemorySaver`
  in dev, keyed so HITL gate pauses survive a restart.

- Prototype validation — [static_check.py](../../backend/app/agents/static_check.py) (stdlib-only structural check: nav↔section, routes
  map, handlers) and [render_check.py](../../backend/app/agents/render_check.py) (headless Chromium: console/nav errors) share
  [route_table.py](../../backend/app/agents/route_table.py)'s pure route resolver so both validators judge the same target page for a
  given nav route; both degrade to a skip rather than a hard failure when a dependency is
  missing. `validators/{html_static,html_render,design_quality}.py` re-wrap the same two
  checks as registered `CapabilityRegistry` `Validator`s for the newer capability-driven path.

- Chat & handoff — [chat_runner.ChatRunner](../../backend/app/agents/chat_runner.py) reproduces the deleted legacy
  `AgentOrchestrator`'s multi-phase (Discovery→...→Preview) event contract byte-for-byte,
  built from 7 text-only `DeepAgentRunner`s; [chat_narrator.py](../../backend/app/agents/chat_narrator.py) is a separate, pure
  event→`chat_reply`-card projector (zero model calls) for the down-channel; [chat/concierge.py](../../backend/app/agents/chat/concierge.py)
  is a distinct, newer per-run capability (`chat:concierge`) that answers questions about a run
  and emits propose-only intents, also built strictly on `DeepAgentRunner`.
  `handoff/{coder,test_agent,compliance_agent,classifier}.py` back `/flowin-handoff`:
  `HandoffCoder` (aliased `CodingAgent`) runs on `DeepAgentRunner`; the test/compliance agents
  and the classifier use the lighter `cached_invoke` one-shot path.

- Support — [types.py](../../backend/app/agents/types.py) (`TokenUsage`, `WorkflowState`), [llm_errors.py](../../backend/app/agents/llm_errors.py) (Bedrock exception →
  `{message, code, recoverable}` for the frontend), [skills.py](../../backend/app/agents/skills.py) / [prompt_overrides.py](../../backend/app/agents/prompt_overrides.py)
  (per-user file-based prompt customization with prompt-injection scrubbing), [modes.py](../../backend/app/agents/modes.py)
  (legacy chat-mode prompt enhancers), [mcp/client.py](../../backend/app/agents/mcp/client.py) (outbound MCP tool client),
  [repo_index/index.py](../../backend/app/agents/repo_index/index.py) (optional tree-sitter symbol index, app-side only so the kernel never
  imports `tree_sitter`), [tools/runner_tools.py](../../backend/app/agents/tools/runner_tools.py) (`report_task_complete`, `spawn_subagents` —
  store-free tools whose call/result events the engine derives progress from).

## Why this shape

`DeepAgentRunner`'s event vocabulary is a deliberate reproduction of the pre-migration
runtime's contract (chunk/usage/tool_call/tool_result/done/gate/error) so the engine and the
frontend needed zero changes when the underlying agent implementation swapped to `deepagents`
— the seam is the streaming interface, not any shared base class.

The two-path model funnel (`DeepAgentRunner` for anything tool-capable or graph-shaped,
`cached_invoke` for one-shot text) is **invariant INV-13, enforced by a banned-pattern CI
test**, specifically to prevent a bespoke `build_model().ainvoke(...)` bypass from
reappearing — one already was deleted and rebuilt as `HandoffCoder`.

Several submodules (`validators/*`, [runtime/local.py](../../backend/app/agents/runtime/local.py), `repo_index/`, [chat/concierge.py](../../backend/app/agents/chat/concierge.py))
are `CapabilityRegistry`-registered plugins that live app-side purely because they need a
heavy dependency (Playwright, tree-sitter, git subprocess, the `DeepAgentRunner` adapter
itself). They import the kernel's port (`agents.capabilities.base`/`registry`) so the
dependency points one way — **the kernel/execution-engine never imports `app.*` directly** —
discovering them only by the registry importing these packages at `discover()` time
(import-linter enforced).

The legacy free-chat stack (`orchestrator.py` / `base.py` / `deep_agent.py`) has already been
deleted by the time of this snapshot (migration Phases 7b/7c) — [chat_runner.ChatRunner](../../backend/app/agents/chat_runner.py) is
its full replacement, kept behaviorally byte-identical via a frozen golden test rather than
reusing any of the old class hierarchy.

`RunSandbox` and its child-workspace facades (`_ChildSandbox` in [runtime/local.py](../../backend/app/agents/runtime/local.py)) repeat the
same traversal-proof `path_for()` pattern independently in each place disk isolation is needed,
rather than a shared base, because each is rooted differently (per-run vs. per-task-worker vs.
git worktree).

Prototype validation is deliberately two-tier — `static_check` (cheap, stdlib, runs after every
build task) plus `render_check` (expensive, real Chromium, catches what static analysis can't)
— both reading through the one [route_table.py](../../backend/app/agents/route_table.py) resolver so they never disagree about which
page a route should activate, and both fail *open* (skip, not error) when their dependency is
absent so CI/dev environments without a browser still work.
